title: How It Works
metaTitle: How Selling Your Mineral Rights Works, Step by Step
metaDescription: The full process for selling mineral or royalty rights to a direct buyer, from first conversation to closing, explained honestly and without pressure.
heroLead: There is no mystery to this process once someone walks you through it in order, which is exactly what almost nobody does upfront.
intro: This page lays out what actually happens between reaching out and closing, in the order it happens, so nothing along the way feels like a surprise. We have sat through this process ourselves as sellers, and the steps below are the ones we wished someone had explained to us clearly the first time.

sections.heading: You Reach Out
paragraphs: Tell us about your interest, whatever you know about it. A deed or a recent royalty statement helps us move faster, but neither is required to start. Plenty of people reach out with only a general sense of what they own, sometimes after inheriting an interest they are still trying to understand, and that is a completely normal starting point.

This step carries no obligation. You can ask questions, request general information, or get a read on a document without committing to anything further. If you are not sure whether what you hold is a mineral interest, a royalty interest, or something narrower, telling us that directly is a fine way to start.

sections.heading: We Research and Build an Offer
paragraphs: We pull publicly available production and permit data for your specific county and combine it with whatever documents you have provided, your deed, your statements, prior offers you have received, to build a documented offer. For producing interests, this means weighing your real royalty history; for non-producing acreage, it means weighing nearby permit activity and where your tract sits within the play.

We can walk you through exactly how we arrived at the number, the decimal, the production or comparable-sale data, and the assumptions used, rather than presenting a figure and asking you to trust it. This is also where our county and basin fluency matters most, since a tract near active permits and one further from any current activity should not be priced the same way.

sections.heading: You Review, Ask Questions, and Compare
paragraphs: Take the time you need. There is no deadline pressure attached to our offers, and we would genuinely rather you get a second opinion, from us reviewing another offer, or from another buyer reviewing ours, than feel rushed into a decision. If anything about the offer or the purchase agreement is unclear, ask; a straightforward explanation should be available for every line.

This is also the point to raise any concerns about your title, an old heirship question, a name discrepancy, a document you cannot locate, so we can address it as part of the process rather than letting it surface unexpectedly later.

sections.heading: Title Review
paragraphs: Once you accept, we order a title review to confirm ownership and identify anything that needs resolving before closing. Clean, well-documented title generally moves fastest. Title with open questions, an unresolved probate, a missing recorded deed, takes longer to clear but is rarely a reason a sale falls through entirely; these issues are common on land that has passed through a family for generations and are typically resolvable with the right curative document.
If a curative step is needed, we will explain what it involves and, depending on the situation, can often help coordinate the fix rather than simply handing the problem back to you to solve alone.

sections.heading: Closing
paragraphs: Closing is typically handled by mail or through mobile and remote online notarization, so travel is generally not required. You will sign the conveyance, we record it with the county, and funds are typically sent shortly after recording. You should receive a copy of the final recorded deed for your own records.

A straightforward transaction with clean title commonly closes within a few weeks of an accepted offer. Where title work is more involved, we will tell you honestly what that means for your specific timeline rather than giving you a number that does not hold up.

faqs.question: Do you need a deed or statement in hand before you contact you?
faqs.answer: No. Sending what you have is enough to start the conversation, and missing documents can typically be located together as part of the process.

faqs.question: Is there a deadline attached to your offers?
faqs.answer: No. We would rather you take the time you need to review the offer and compare it against other options than feel pressured into a fast decision.

faqs.question: What happens if a title issue turns up during review?
faqs.answer: Most title issues, like an old unrecorded deed or an unresolved heirship question, are routine to resolve with a curative document rather than being reasons the sale falls through. We will walk you through what is needed.

faqs.question: Will you need to travel to close?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Closing is typically handled by mail or mobile and remote online notarization, so you can complete the process from wherever you live.

faqs.question: How soon after closing do you receive payment?
faqs.answer: Funds are typically sent shortly after the deed is recorded with the county. Exact timing can vary slightly depending on the county's recording process.
